lessons.title: Metrics
lessons.summary: Metrics are numeric measurements aggregated over time with identifying labels or dimensions.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Metrics are numeric measurements aggregated over time with identifying labels or dimensions.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: They efficiently show trends and support alerts, but aggregation discards individual event detail. Choose units, temporality and label cardinality deliberately. A metric name without a definition and population is easy to misinterpret.

lessons.takeaway: They efficiently show trends and support alerts, but aggregation discards individual event detail. Choose units, temporality and label cardinality deliberately. A metric name without a definition and population is easy to misinterpret.

lessons.title: Logs
lessons.summary: Logs record discrete events with contextual fields and timestamps.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Logs record discrete events with contextual fields and timestamps.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Structured fields make filtering and correlation more reliable than parsing inconsistent text. Include useful identifiers while excluding credentials and unnecessary personal data. Sampling, buffering and retention determine which events remain available.

lessons.takeaway: Structured fields make filtering and correlation more reliable than parsing inconsistent text. Include useful identifiers while excluding credentials and unnecessary personal data. Sampling, buffering and retention determine which events remain available.

lessons.title: Traces
lessons.summary: Distributed traces connect spans describing work across a request's path.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Distributed traces connect spans describing work across a request's path.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Parent-child and causal links reveal where time is spent and which dependencies participate. Instrumentation and sampling may omit parts of the path. A trace is evidence of one observed execution, not a complete population-level latency distribution.

lessons.takeaway: Parent-child and causal links reveal where time is spent and which dependencies participate. Instrumentation and sampling may omit parts of the path. A trace is evidence of one observed execution, not a complete population-level latency distribution.

lessons.title: Counters
lessons.summary: A counter accumulates occurrences or quantities and normally increases until it resets.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A counter accumulates occurrences or quantities and normally increases until it resets.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Use a reset-aware rate or increase calculation for interval behavior. Summing raw counters from restarting instances can produce misleading results. Define exactly which event increments the counter and avoid double counting retries as unique users.

lessons.takeaway: Use a reset-aware rate or increase calculation for interval behavior. Summing raw counters from restarting instances can produce misleading results. Define exactly which event increments the counter and avoid double counting retries as unique users.

lessons.title: Gauges
lessons.summary: A gauge reports a value that can rise or fall, such as queue depth or current memory usage.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A gauge reports a value that can rise or fall, such as queue depth or current memory usage.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It represents a sampled state rather than an accumulated event count. A rate calculation intended for counters may not be meaningful on a gauge. Sampling frequency can miss short peaks, so choose collection intervals around the use case.

lessons.takeaway: It represents a sampled state rather than an accumulated event count. A rate calculation intended for counters may not be meaningful on a gauge. Sampling frequency can miss short peaks, so choose collection intervals around the use case.

lessons.title: Histograms
lessons.summary: Histograms record a distribution using buckets and count or sum information.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Histograms record a distribution using buckets and count or sum information.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Bucket boundaries determine resolution near important thresholds. Classic Prometheus histogram buckets are cumulative and support aggregation before estimating quantiles. The estimate is limited by bucket design; it is not an exact percentile of retained raw events.

lessons.takeaway: Bucket boundaries determine resolution near important thresholds. Classic Prometheus histogram buckets are cumulative and support aggregation before estimating quantiles. The estimate is limited by bucket design; it is not an exact percentile of retained raw events.

lessons.title: Labels
lessons.summary: Labels distinguish metric time series by dimensions such as service, route or status.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Labels distinguish metric time series by dimensions such as service, route or status.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Every distinct label combination creates another series. Unbounded request IDs or user IDs can overwhelm storage and query capacity. Use bounded dimensions for metrics and put high-cardinality event detail in appropriately controlled logs or traces.

lessons.takeaway: Every distinct label combination creates another series. Unbounded request IDs or user IDs can overwhelm storage and query capacity. Use bounded dimensions for metrics and put high-cardinality event detail in appropriately controlled logs or traces.

lessons.title: Dashboards
lessons.summary: Dashboards organize signals to answer operational questions.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Dashboards organize signals to answer operational questions.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Start with user outcomes, then expose dependency and resource diagnostics. Show units, time windows and missing-data behavior. A visually green dashboard is not meaningful if it omits the failing user path or averages away a regional outage.

lessons.takeaway: Start with user outcomes, then expose dependency and resource diagnostics. Show units, time windows and missing-data behavior. A visually green dashboard is not meaningful if it omits the failing user path or averages away a regional outage.

lessons.title: Rate before aggregation
lessons.summary: Reset-aware rate calculation should be applied to individual counter series before they are aggregated.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Reset-aware rate calculation should be applied to individual counter series before they are aggregated.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Otherwise one instance's reset can be hidden by another instance's increasing value. In PromQL, sum(rate(counter[window])) preserves per-series reset handling. Choose a window long enough to contain useful samples.

lessons.takeaway: Otherwise one instance's reset can be hidden by another instance's increasing value. In PromQL, sum(rate(counter[window])) preserves per-series reset handling. Choose a window long enough to contain useful samples.

lessons.title: Percentiles
lessons.summary: A percentile describes a value below which a specified share of observations falls.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A percentile describes a value below which a specified share of observations falls.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The p99 is not a maximum and cannot generally be combined by averaging instance p99 values. Aggregate suitable distributions first, then estimate the percentile. Sparse samples and different populations can make tail estimates unstable.

lessons.takeaway: The p99 is not a maximum and cannot generally be combined by averaging instance p99 values. Aggregate suitable distributions first, then estimate the percentile. Sparse samples and different populations can make tail estimates unstable.

lessons.title: Missing data
lessons.summary: Missing telemetry means a measurement was not observed, which is different from observing zero.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Missing telemetry means a measurement was not observed, which is different from observing zero.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Collection failure, discovery changes, label changes or an idle system can cause gaps. Define alert behavior explicitly and monitor the telemetry pipeline itself. Treating absent errors as zero errors can falsely declare an unobserved service healthy.

lessons.takeaway: Collection failure, discovery changes, label changes or an idle system can cause gaps. Define alert behavior explicitly and monitor the telemetry pipeline itself. Treating absent errors as zero errors can falsely declare an unobserved service healthy.

lessons.title: Scrape health
lessons.summary: Scrape health describes whether a metrics collector can discover and retrieve target data.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Scrape health describes whether a metrics collector can discover and retrieve target data.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A successful scrape indicates collection worked, not that the application is healthy. Inspect target errors, duration and sample volume. A target can disappear from discovery entirely, requiring separate expected-target checks.

lessons.takeaway: A successful scrape indicates collection worked, not that the application is healthy. Inspect target errors, duration and sample volume. A target can disappear from discovery entirely, requiring separate expected-target checks.

lessons.title: Recording rules
lessons.summary: Recording rules precompute query results into new time series.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Recording rules precompute query results into new time series.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: They reduce repeated query cost and standardize shared calculations. Evaluation interval and dependency order influence freshness. Version and test rule changes because a wrong recording rule can spread incorrect results across many dashboards and alerts.

lessons.takeaway: They reduce repeated query cost and standardize shared calculations. Evaluation interval and dependency order influence freshness. Version and test rule changes because a wrong recording rule can spread incorrect results across many dashboards and alerts.

lessons.title: Alert duration
lessons.summary: An alert duration requires a condition to remain true for a configured period before firing.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: An alert duration requires a condition to remain true for a configured period before firing.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It reduces noise from short fluctuations but delays detection. Choose it from the tolerated impact and signal behavior, not as a blanket way to hide unstable alerts. Pending and firing states should be understood during tests.

lessons.takeaway: It reduces noise from short fluctuations but delays detection. Choose it from the tolerated impact and signal behavior, not as a blanket way to hide unstable alerts. Pending and firing states should be understood during tests.

lessons.title: Alert grouping
lessons.summary: Alert grouping combines related alerts into fewer notifications.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Alert grouping combines related alerts into fewer notifications.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Grouping keys should preserve the information needed to assign ownership and act. Overly broad grouping can hide independent incidents; overly narrow grouping creates floods. Grouping changes notification presentation, not the underlying alert condition.

lessons.takeaway: Grouping keys should preserve the information needed to assign ownership and act. Overly broad grouping can hide independent incidents; overly narrow grouping creates floods. Grouping changes notification presentation, not the underlying alert condition.

lessons.title: Alert inhibition
lessons.summary: Inhibition suppresses notifications for selected alerts when a related source alert is active.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Inhibition suppresses notifications for selected alerts when a related source alert is active.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: For example, a cluster outage can suppress many dependent service symptoms. Matching labels must prevent unrelated alerts from being silenced. Test both suppression and release after recovery so important signals do not remain hidden.

lessons.takeaway: For example, a cluster outage can suppress many dependent service symptoms. Matching labels must prevent unrelated alerts from being silenced. Test both suppression and release after recovery so important signals do not remain hidden.

lessons.title: Sampling
lessons.summary: Sampling retains a subset of telemetry to control cost and processing overhead.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Sampling retains a subset of telemetry to control cost and processing overhead.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Head sampling decides near the start of a trace and is inexpensive but may miss rare failures. The sampled population can be biased. Do not infer exact request counts from sampled traces without understanding the sampling method.

lessons.takeaway: Head sampling decides near the start of a trace and is inexpensive but may miss rare failures. The sampled population can be biased. Do not infer exact request counts from sampled traces without understanding the sampling method.

lessons.title: Tail sampling
lessons.summary: Tail sampling waits for enough trace information to choose traces based on completed behavior.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Tail sampling waits for enough trace information to choose traces based on completed behavior.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It can favor errors or slow requests but requires buffering and trace-consistent routing. Late spans, memory pressure and incomplete traces affect decisions. Size the collector and define behavior when sampling capacity is exceeded.

lessons.takeaway: It can favor errors or slow requests but requires buffering and trace-consistent routing. Late spans, memory pressure and incomplete traces affect decisions. Size the collector and define behavior when sampling capacity is exceeded.

lessons.title: Context propagation
lessons.summary: Context propagation carries trace and related identifiers across process boundaries.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Context propagation carries trace and related identifiers across process boundaries.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: HTTP headers or message metadata let downstream spans join the same trace. Instrument both sender and receiver and preserve context through asynchronous work. Trust boundaries must prevent arbitrary inbound context from becoming an authorization signal.

lessons.takeaway: HTTP headers or message metadata let downstream spans join the same trace. Instrument both sender and receiver and preserve context through asynchronous work. Trust boundaries must prevent arbitrary inbound context from becoming an authorization signal.

lessons.title: Correlation
lessons.summary: Correlation connects signals using shared attributes such as trace ID, service identity and time.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Correlation connects signals using shared attributes such as trace ID, service identity and time.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A log linked to a trace can explain a slow span while metrics show prevalence. Correlated timing alone does not establish causation. Check whether populations, clocks and deployment versions align before drawing conclusions.

lessons.takeaway: A log linked to a trace can explain a slow span while metrics show prevalence. Correlated timing alone does not establish causation. Check whether populations, clocks and deployment versions align before drawing conclusions.

lessons.title: Sensitive telemetry
lessons.summary: Telemetry can contain credentials, personal information and business-sensitive payloads.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Telemetry can contain credentials, personal information and business-sensitive payloads.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Collect only useful fields, redact at the source where possible and restrict access and retention. A later dashboard mask does not remove data already stored. Review exception messages, URLs and high-cardinality attributes for accidental disclosure.

lessons.takeaway: Collect only useful fields, redact at the source where possible and restrict access and retention. A later dashboard mask does not remove data already stored. Review exception messages, URLs and high-cardinality attributes for accidental disclosure.

lessons.title: Retention
lessons.summary: Retention defines how long telemetry is kept and at what resolution.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Retention defines how long telemetry is kept and at what resolution.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Longer retention supports historical investigations but costs storage and increases exposure. Downsampling preserves some trends while losing detail. Align retention with incident response needs and ensure deletion policies cover backups and derived datasets where required.

lessons.takeaway: Longer retention supports historical investigations but costs storage and increases exposure. Downsampling preserves some trends while losing detail. Align retention with incident response needs and ensure deletion policies cover backups and derived datasets where required.

lessons.title: Telemetry pipelines
lessons.summary: A telemetry pipeline receives, processes and exports signals between applications and backends.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A telemetry pipeline receives, processes and exports signals between applications and backends.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Queues, batching, retries and memory limits affect reliability under backpressure. A blocked exporter can exhaust collector memory or drop data. Monitor queue age, refused data and export failures independently of application metrics.

lessons.takeaway: Queues, batching, retries and memory limits affect reliability under backpressure. A blocked exporter can exhaust collector memory or drop data. Monitor queue age, refused data and export failures independently of application metrics.

lessons.title: Resource identity
lessons.summary: Resource attributes identify the entity producing telemetry, such as service, environment and instance.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Resource attributes identify the entity producing telemetry, such as service, environment and instance.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Consistent identity enables correct grouping across metrics, logs and traces. A changing or missing service name can fragment a dashboard. Avoid using unstable instance identifiers where a stable service-level aggregation is intended.

lessons.takeaway: Consistent identity enables correct grouping across metrics, logs and traces. A changing or missing service name can fragment a dashboard. Avoid using unstable instance identifiers where a stable service-level aggregation is intended.

lessons.title: Clock skew
lessons.summary: Clock skew is disagreement between clocks used to timestamp events.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Clock skew is disagreement between clocks used to timestamp events.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It can make cross-host logs appear out of order and distort apparent span timing. Synchronize wall clocks and use causal IDs and monotonic durations where appropriate. Do not infer a negative processing duration is an application behavior without checking clocks.

lessons.takeaway: It can make cross-host logs appear out of order and distort apparent span timing. Synchronize wall clocks and use causal IDs and monotonic durations where appropriate. Do not infer a negative processing duration is an application behavior without checking clocks.

lessons.title: RED signals
lessons.summary: RED tracks request rate, errors and duration for request-driven services.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: RED tracks request rate, errors and duration for request-driven services.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It starts diagnosis from demand, success and user-perceived speed. Define what counts as a request and error for the service. Pair RED with resource and dependency signals when investigating the cause.

lessons.takeaway: It starts diagnosis from demand, success and user-perceived speed. Define what counts as a request and error for the service. Pair RED with resource and dependency signals when investigating the cause.

lessons.title: USE signals
lessons.summary: USE examines utilization, saturation and errors for each resource.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: USE examines utilization, saturation and errors for each resource.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: CPU busy time, runnable queues and hardware errors answer different questions. High utilization without saturation may be acceptable; a queue can reveal a bottleneck before average utilization looks extreme. Inventory relevant resources rather than checking CPU alone.

lessons.takeaway: CPU busy time, runnable queues and hardware errors answer different questions. High utilization without saturation may be acceptable; a queue can reveal a bottleneck before average utilization looks extreme. Inventory relevant resources rather than checking CPU alone.

lessons.title: Synthetic checks
lessons.summary: Synthetic checks execute controlled probes of selected user paths.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Synthetic checks execute controlled probes of selected user paths.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: They can detect failures before organic traffic arrives and test outside-in availability. Probe location, credentials and test data determine coverage. A simple health endpoint cannot represent a full checkout or login transaction.

lessons.takeaway: They can detect failures before organic traffic arrives and test outside-in availability. Probe location, credentials and test data determine coverage. A simple health endpoint cannot represent a full checkout or login transaction.

lessons.title: Instrumentation cost
lessons.summary: Instrumentation consumes CPU, memory, network and backend capacity.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Instrumentation consumes CPU, memory, network and backend capacity.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: High event volume, expensive labels and synchronous export can affect the application being measured. Bound overhead, batch exports and test under load. More telemetry is useful only when it improves decisions at an acceptable cost.

lessons.takeaway: High event volume, expensive labels and synchronous export can affect the application being measured. Bound overhead, batch exports and test under load. More telemetry is useful only when it improves decisions at an acceptable cost.

lessons.title: Evidence and causality
lessons.summary: Observability evidence supports hypotheses about why a system behaves as it does.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Observability evidence supports hypotheses about why a system behaves as it does.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Compare affected and unaffected cohorts, align changes with the timeline and test predictions. A graph moving at the same time as an outage is a clue, not proof. Record uncertainty and seek evidence that could disprove the leading hypothesis.

lessons.takeaway: Compare affected and unaffected cohorts, align changes with the timeline and test predictions. A graph moving at the same time as an outage is a clue, not proof. Record uncertainty and seek evidence that could disprove the leading hypothesis.

commands.title: Scrape availability
commands.definition: A PromQL selector returns the latest scrape-success signal for matching targets.
commands.purpose: Check whether the collector can currently retrieve target metrics.
commands.environment: PromQL query, not shell. Scrape health is not application health.
commands.interpretation: 1 means a successful scrape and 0 a failed scrape; missing targets may produce no series.
commands.safety: PromQL query, not shell. Scrape health is not application health.

commands.title: Counter rate
commands.definition: Calculates a reset-aware per-second rate for each counter series.
commands.purpose: Turn a cumulative request counter into recent throughput.
commands.environment: Illustrative metric; use a window with enough samples for the scrape interval.
commands.interpretation: Each result retains source labels; apply rate before aggregating different instances.
commands.safety: Illustrative metric; use a window with enough samples for the scrape interval.

commands.title: Aggregated throughput
commands.definition: Aggregates per-series request rates by service job.
commands.purpose: Compare service traffic without averaging raw counters.
commands.environment: PromQL; label names and counting semantics must match instrumentation.
commands.interpretation: One output series per job shows requests per second across instances.
commands.safety: PromQL; label names and counting semantics must match instrumentation.

commands.title: Error ratio
commands.definition: Computes a ratio of server-error requests to total requests.
commands.purpose: Monitor a defined failure population alongside traffic.
commands.environment: PromQL example; 5xx-only may omit business failures or client-visible timeouts.
commands.interpretation: 0.02 means 2% under this definition; absent traffic requires separate interpretation.
commands.safety: PromQL example; 5xx-only may omit business failures or client-visible timeouts.

commands.title: Classic histogram p95
commands.definition: Estimates p95 latency from cumulative classic histogram buckets.
commands.purpose: Inspect the slow tail across instances.
commands.environment: PromQL for classic histograms; native histogram syntax and semantics differ.
commands.interpretation: Result is seconds; le must remain in aggregation and bucket layout limits precision.
commands.safety: PromQL for classic histograms; native histogram syntax and semantics differ.

commands.title: Mean latency
commands.definition: Divides observed duration accumulation by observation count.
commands.purpose: Compare mean latency with tail behavior.
commands.environment: PromQL; requires matching sum/count series and a nonempty population.
commands.interpretation: The unit is seconds per observation; a healthy mean can coexist with a bad p99.
commands.safety: PromQL; requires matching sum/count series and a nonempty population.

commands.title: Absent target signal
commands.definition: Returns a signal when no matching series exists.
commands.purpose: Detect disappearance from discovery rather than only failed scrapes.
commands.environment: PromQL; use expected-target inventory for per-instance absence rather than this service-wide check alone.
commands.interpretation: A returned 1 means the selector has no series; an empty result means at least one match exists.
commands.safety: PromQL; use expected-target inventory for per-instance absence rather than this service-wide check alone.

commands.title: Counter resets
commands.definition: Counts observed decreases in a counter over one hour.
commands.purpose: Correlate rate changes with restarts or instrumentation resets.
commands.environment: PromQL; resets are not automatically application failures.
commands.interpretation: A positive result identifies resets within that series; replacement labels can instead create a new series.
commands.safety: PromQL; resets are not automatically application failures.

commands.title: Configuration validation
commands.definition: Validates Prometheus configuration and referenced rule files.
commands.purpose: Catch invalid configuration before a controlled reload.
commands.environment: Local validation; use a trusted configuration and installed promtool matching deployment expectations.
commands.expectedOutput: SUCCESS: prometheus.yml is valid prometheus config file syntax
commands.interpretation: SUCCESS indicates accepted syntax and referenced-file checks, not target reachability.
commands.safety: Local validation; use a trusted configuration and installed promtool matching deployment expectations.

commands.title: Rule validation
commands.definition: Checks recording and alerting rule syntax.
commands.purpose: Find invalid expressions before publishing rules.
commands.environment: Local read-only validation; add rule tests for behavioral expectations.
commands.interpretation: Read file and rule errors; a valid expression can still measure the wrong population.
commands.safety: Local read-only validation; add rule tests for behavioral expectations.

commands.title: Rule unit tests
commands.definition: Runs rule tests against supplied input series and expected results.
commands.purpose: Verify alert timing and query behavior under resets, gaps and failures.
commands.environment: Runs local test definitions; fixtures should include missing data and recovery.
commands.interpretation: PASS means the specified cases matched; untested scenarios remain unknown.
commands.safety: Runs local test definitions; fixtures should include missing data and recovery.

commands.title: Metrics endpoint sample
commands.definition: Retrieves a local Prometheus-format metrics endpoint.
commands.purpose: Check that exposition exists and inspect metric names and labels.
commands.environment: Read-only HTTP request; endpoint and port are examples and output may expose infrastructure metadata.
commands.interpretation: HELP and TYPE describe metric families; sample labels define individual series.
commands.safety: Read-only HTTP request; endpoint and port are examples and output may expose infrastructure metadata.

debugging.title: Dashboard green during outage
debugging.symptom: The application is unavailable but the dashboard shows no errors.

steps.evidence: Check whether telemetry is missing, targets disappeared or the error population excludes timeouts. Compare an outside-in request with scrape health and discovery.
Repair collection or the SLI definition, and add explicit missing-data detection. Do not turn missing series into zero errors without justification.
Simulate both application failure and telemetry loss; verify each produces the intended distinct signal.

references.title: Dashboard green during outage — primary documentation

debugging.title: Cardinality explosion
debugging.symptom: Metrics storage memory and ingestion volume spike after a release.

steps.evidence: Inspect newly added labels and series growth. User IDs, request IDs or raw URLs can create unbounded combinations even when metric syntax is valid.
Remove or bound high-cardinality labels at instrumentation or ingestion, preserving useful aggregates. Control rollout and cleanup according to backend behavior.
Compare series count, ingestion pressure and query latency after the change while confirming important dimensions remain available.

debugging.title: Incorrect aggregate p99
debugging.symptom: A dashboard averages instance p99 values and reports misleading latency.

steps.evidence: Compare traffic weights and bucket populations across instances. Percentiles are not generally composable by arithmetic averaging.
Aggregate compatible histogram distributions before estimating a service percentile, or use an explicitly defined threshold SLI.
Test with uneven traffic and latency distributions and compare the query with known expected behavior.

debugging.title: Rate spike after restart
debugging.symptom: A counter chart shows a huge spike or negative result after a process restart.

steps.evidence: Check whether raw differences or aggregation were applied before reset-aware rate calculation. Also inspect changing instance labels.
Apply rate per counter series before aggregation and use an appropriate sample window. Correct instrumentation if the metric is not actually a counter.
Test restart fixtures and verify the calculated request rate remains consistent with generated traffic.

references.title: Rate spike after restart — primary documentation

debugging.title: Alert never fires
debugging.symptom: An obvious sustained error does not produce a notification.

steps.evidence: Separate rule loading, expression results, pending duration, routing, silences and inhibition. A valid rule file does not prove the expression matches labels.
Correct the specific broken stage and add rule and routing tests. Avoid removing all inhibition globally without understanding dependencies.
Inject a controlled test condition and verify firing, recipient routing and resolution notifications within expected timing.

debugging.title: Alert flood during shared failure
debugging.symptom: A database incident generates hundreds of dependent-service notifications.

steps.evidence: Identify common dependency and labels used for grouping and inhibition. Confirm independent incidents would remain distinguishable.
Group related alerts and introduce narrowly matched inhibition for dependency symptoms while keeping the primary actionable alert visible.
Test shared and unrelated failures together, then recovery, to ensure suppression is scoped and released correctly.

references.title: Alert flood during shared failure — primary documentation

debugging.title: Broken distributed trace
debugging.symptom: Frontend spans exist but downstream work appears as unrelated traces.

steps.evidence: Inspect propagation headers or message metadata at each boundary and instrumentation compatibility. Check asynchronous context handling and sampling decisions.
Propagate supported trace context through clients, servers and queues without using it as authorization. Align resource identity and sampling policy.
Execute a known multi-service request and verify causal span relationships and correlated logs across the full path.

debugging.title: Collector drops data
debugging.symptom: Telemetry gaps appear during peak traffic while applications stay healthy.

steps.evidence: Inspect collector queue, export-failure, refused-data and memory signals using the deployed collector's actual metric names. Check backend throttling and network failures.
Bound queues and memory, tune batching/retries and restore exporter capacity. Reduce low-value volume if necessary rather than allowing unbounded buffering.
Run a controlled peak and confirm bounded memory, acceptable queue age and no unexpected data loss.

debugging.title: Sensitive values in traces
debugging.symptom: Trace attributes contain access tokens or personal payloads.

steps.evidence: Identify the instrumentation field and every downstream storage/export path. Review the trace collector and SDK configuration directly, using restricted access to representative telemetry.
Stop collection of the sensitive field, rotate exposed credentials where relevant and remove retained data under policy. Prefer source-side minimization.
Use a safe sentinel value in a test request and verify it does not reach spans, logs or exports.

references.title: Sensitive values in traces — primary documentation

debugging.title: Causal conclusion from coincident graph
debugging.symptom: A team blames CPU because it rose near the incident.

steps.evidence: Align populations, time windows and deployments; compare affected and unaffected instances. CPU may be a consequence of retries rather than the initiating cause.
Test a bounded hypothesis with predicted outcomes and collect disconfirming evidence. Mitigate user impact while preserving uncertainty in the incident record.
Confirm the proposed cause explains the timeline and cohort differences and that the targeted fix changes the predicted signals.

references.title: Causal conclusion from coincident graph — primary documentation
